evidence_items.explanation: The experiments support a substantial role for more training data, including a smaller model trained on more tokens outperforming larger predecessors. They do not establish that data quantity predominantly caused the entire set of gains Marcus discusses; the paper also reports changes in the final model's training setup.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI attributes these gains to supervised demonstrations and preference-based reinforcement learning applied to GPT-3, using little additional data relative to pretraining. This challenges the proposed explanation for this particular successor, but cannot determine the primary cause of all the improvements under discussion.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved study apportions the relevant cross-generation gains among data quantity, parameter count, compute and training methods.
The studies measure different outcomes: pretraining loss, downstream benchmark performance and instruction-following preferences.
The word primarily cannot be settled merely by showing that more data helps or that an alternative method also helps.
